project.name: Policy Text Lab
project.description: Policy Text Lab is a full-stack platform for computational text research, supporting corpus management, human annotation, reliability analysis, quantitative analysis, supervised classification, topic modeling, and reproducible exports. Built with a modular FastAPI backend and React frontend, backed by PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, and Celery workers. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the project README to understand Policy Text Lab's research workflow, modular architecture, and local development stack. It gives the vocabulary for the rest of the tour: corpora, annotation, reliability, classification, and reproducible exports.

tour.title: FastAPI Startup
tour.description: The FastAPI entry point establishes the application lifecycle and brings the backend's routers and shared services together. Read it next to see where HTTP delivery begins before following requests into the modular backend.

tour.title: Runtime Configuration
tour.description: Configuration is the most widely depended-on backend foundation, so it is worth understanding before feature code. This module centralizes settings that determine connections, security, observability, and service behavior across the application.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic-style settings keep environment-derived configuration typed and centralized, which makes startup validation and deployment behavior easier to reason about.

tour.title: Request Dependencies
tour.description: Database request dependencies connect API handling to the persistence layer without making every route manage sessions directly. This is the bridge from FastAPI's delivery layer to the bounded-context modules introduced next.

tour.title: Research Workflows
tour.description: The text-research routes are the broadest backend feature surface, coordinating corpus, annotation, analysis, classification, and export operations. Their domain models define the research concepts and persisted entities those endpoints work with.

tour.title: Database Bootstrap
tour.description: The local database setup script shows the persistence prerequisites underlying the backend modules. Review it after the domain layer to connect application entities and repositories to the PostgreSQL environment used during development.
tour.languageLesson: SQL setup and migration scripts make database state explicit; keeping schema evolution alongside application code makes local environments reproducible.

tour.title: Frontend Bootstrap
tour.description: The React entry point starts the client application and establishes the browser-side shell for the research workspace. It is the natural transition from backend capabilities to the interface through which researchers use them.
tour.languageLesson: React applications bootstrap by rendering a root component into the page, then compose views and providers around that root.

tour.title: Client Research API
tour.description: The text-research client API is the frontend counterpart to the backend feature routes. Its high fan-out makes it a useful map of the requests that frontend views issue while users progress through research workflows.

tour.title: Verification Strategy
tour.description: The authentication API tests demonstrate the repository's automated verification layer and provide concrete examples of exercising HTTP behavior. Use them to understand how changes to the delivery and configuration steps are protected from regressions.

tour.title: Local Operations
tour.description: Finish with the local operations definitions that orchestrate PostgreSQL, Redis, and supporting services around the application. The Makefile provides repeatable developer commands, while Docker Compose supplies the service topology needed by the backend and workers.
tour.languageLesson: Compose expresses service dependencies and shared networks declaratively, while Make targets provide memorable, repeatable entry points for local workflows.

tour.title: Architecture Decisions
tour.description: The modular-monolith decision record explains why the backend is organized into bounded contexts rather than independent deployable services. Revisit it after the code tour to connect the implementation boundaries to their intended long-term architectural constraints.
